name: bead-to-prod
description: BLUEPRINT carrier-class reference (validated cold, no author-run receipt — the lanes name YOUR tracker and repo conventions): a work-item-to-PR-open pipeline at full carrier scale — law in defaults.context, a complementary premise-gate pair, detached-lap testing, blind tiered review through a join, a policy judge on after_partial, a stand-down terminal for dead premises, and a fail-closed MACHINE exit-check. THE RULES THIS SHAPE ENCODES: (1) CLOSEOUT LAW — the graph ends at PR-open; whoever merges closes the record ONCE with the merge cite in the reason, and a seat holding the closeout may not end its turn without attempting it (a soft note is not a receipt; merged-but-unclosed is the defect this law exists to catch). (2) PREMISE-FIRST — intake re-reads the record and judges the premise BEFORE any code is written; a dead premise takes the stand-down terminal, never a half-build. (3) COMMIT BEFORE VERIFY — a verify receipt printed against a dirty tree is not a receipt. (4) RECEIPT TERMINATOR — a trailing non-zero tool call harvests a valid answer as a dead lane; append a trailing '; true' (append, never wrap a chain with ||). (5) WALL WINDOWS — any probe expected to run past ~120s is launched detached and waited on, never foreground-polled. (6) FAIL-CLOSED EXIT-CHECK — the run may not end greener than the checkout it found: a machine gate compares a worktree snapshot taken at intake against live status and only releases on empty diff; a machine timeout is a failure, not an approval. run_context seeds (ALL required): 'item' = the work record (id or path); 'repo_dir' = a lane-dedicated pre-provisioned git worktree (never the shared main checkout); 'trunk_remote' = the remote to diff and PR against. Blueprints are validated, not proven: smoke-run it against one real item before trusting it with your queue.

defaults.context:
You are one node in a bead-to-prod carrier. Binding rules for every seat:
- The tracker record as committed is truth; re-read it — the triggering event is a trigger only.
- CLOSEOUT LAW: a merge-class close carries the merge cite in the reason; never close a fix whose commit is not on the trunk via a merged PR; an unlanded fix is an open record.
- Treat existing branch/worktree state as input to verify and continue, never permission to overwrite.
- Never print secrets, rewrite history, push the trunk, or improvise destructive actions.
- Finish with only the required fenced JSON and exit 0; stop every child/background process before finishing; append a trailing '; true' to your final shell command (RECEIPT TERMINATOR).

nodes.goal: Intake gate only for record {run.item} — no planning re-derivation: the promote/authoring pass already committed symptom, root cause, bounded fix scope and Acceptance to the record body; re-planning at intake was measured as restatement. FIRST actions, batched: (1) snapshot the checkout's pre-lane state so the exit-check only reddens what THIS lane caused: `git -C {run.repo_dir} status --porcelain --untracked-files=all > ./checkout.baseline` (the exit-check gate re-reads this file from the run dir); (2) verify {run.repo_dir} is a real linked worktree; (3) re-read the record and probe its premise read-only. Verdict rules: the premise is 'valid' only after that probe; invalid or inconclusive must stop implementation. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"item": "{run.item}", "verdict": "ready|blocked", "premise_verdict": "valid|invalid|inconclusive", "premise_evidence": "<what the probe showed>", "premise_delta": "<one line: a real discovery beyond the record body; empty when none>", "branch": "<branch this lane will own>", "sha": "<current base sha>"}

premise_verdict.description: valid only after a probe; invalid/inconclusive stop the build

nodes.goal: Implementation seat. Read claim_plan from your inputs. Work ONLY in the prepared worktree {run.repo_dir} on the claim_plan branch. COMMIT BEFORE VERIFY: commit before launching any verify; never verify a dirty tree. If claim_plan verdict/premise are not ready/valid, make no edits and return verdict=blocked. Produce a cross-stage digest so review seats read your handoff instead of re-discovering the diff. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "built|blocked", "branch": "<sha>", "sha": "<head sha>", "diffstat": "<one line>", "changed_lines": <int added+deleted vs {run.trunk_remote} trunk>, "tree_clean": true|false, "digest": {"changed_files": ["<path>"], "test_cmd": "<how to re-run it>", "gotchas": "<landmines>"}, "notes": "<one line>"}

changed_lines.description: lines added+deleted vs trunk; tiers the second review seat

nodes.goal: Deterministic test seat — you run checks, you do not judge design. If build.verdict is not 'built', reply the SCHEMA-COMPLETE no-op {"verdict":"no-op","stages":"stand-down: build verdict=<verdict>, no build to test","failures":[],"committed":false} and stop (a schema-incomplete reply dies the lane at validation — a real lane lost a full run to exactly this). Otherwise re-run the digest's test_cmd on the committed head sha. Checks longer than ~120s: launch detached and wait on it, never foreground-poll (WALL WINDOWS). Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "pass|fail|no-op", "stages": "<what ran, on what sha>", "failures": ["<failing check with its one-line error>"], "committed": true|false}

verdict.description: pass (checks green on the committed head), fail (a check is red or nothing was committed), no-op (no build — clean stand-down)

nodes.goal: Fix lane. If test.verdict is 'pass' or 'no-op', change nothing and return verdict=pass. On 'fail': repair the NAMED failing checks in the worktree, re-run, commit; return verdict=pass with the new head sha, or verdict=blocked stating what you cannot fix. A partially-dead lane must still return the schema — name what ran and what did not. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "pass|blocked", "sha": "<new head or empty>", "stages": "<what you re-ran>", "reason": "<what could not be fixed, or empty>"}

Policy judge, read-only. tests_green=true only when the premise is valid, build.verdict is built, test/fix report committed green checks — any blocked/red/missing receipt makes tests_green=false. destructive reflects real reboot/quorum/driver/storage/data risk in the planned change — a normal edit is NOT destructive. stand_down=true when the runtime premise is invalid OR test.verdict is no-op (the no-code close arm may run and stamps the class from your reason). Reply with ONLY fenced json {"tests_green": true|false, "destructive": true|false, "record_touching": true|false, "stand_down": true|false, "reason": "<one line class for the stand-down or green light>"}

Blind code review: inspect only the branch diff against {run.trunk_remote} trunk and the supplied test receipt — read the digest, do not re-discover the diff. Do not edit. Find correctness, safety, data-loss, secret, and contract regressions. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "ready|fix|blocked", "findings": ["<load-bearing file:line finding>"], "minimal_fix": "<smallest correction or empty>", "notes": "<one line>"} — 'ready' only with no load-bearing finding.

Second review seat, diff-tiered in: it joins the review ONLY for diffs of 50+ changed lines (a small diff is single-reviewed; the join below must read this seat's tier-skip as policy, not as a missing review). Same blind rule as the first reviewer: diff vs {run.trunk_remote} trunk, no edits, load-bearing findings only. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "ready|fix|blocked", "findings": ["<load-bearing file:line finding>"], "minimal_fix": "<smallest correction or empty>", "notes": "<one line>"}

Review join. Deduplicate the blind review outputs. A reviewer reading {"agent": "skipped"} is the diff-tier skip — the surviving reviewer IS the full review; never treat a tier-skip as a missing review. A cited load-bearing finding means verdict=fix; an uncited or speculative concern is non-blocking. If either reviewer is blocked, verdict=blocked. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "ready|fix|blocked", "findings": ["<deduped actionable finding>"], "minimal_fix": "<smallest complete change or empty>"}

Apply the review's deduped findings: fix the NAMED issues in the worktree, re-run the digest's test_cmd, commit. Push the branch to {run.trunk_remote} so the PR carries the reviewed head. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "pass|blocked", "sha": "<new head>", "applied": ["<finding you fixed>"], "reason": "<what still needs human eyes, or empty>"}

One seat, two doors: it arrives either through the ready gate (review clean — say so) or behind review_fix (findings applied — re-state the reviewed head sha from review_fix). No edits. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"ready": true|false, "sha": "<reviewed head>", "note": "<one line on which door you came through>"}

Open the PR: push (if review_fix did not already), then open it against {run.trunk_remote} trunk from the reviewed branch. The body carries the receipts: symptom/root-cause/scope from the record, the test stages the test seat ran, the review disposition, and the changed-line count. Do NOT merge — the trunk's checks and the owner's merge own that step; stamp the record with the PR link (comment the URL; the closeout happens once, at merge, with the merge cite). Reply with ONLY fenced json {"opened": true|false, "pr_url": "<url or empty>", "head_sha": "<sha the PR carries>", "notes": "<one line>"}

No-code close arm: this lane reached a terminal WITHOUT a build (dead premise at intake, or policy stand-down). Comment the record with the stand-down class citing claim_plan.premise_evidence (and policy.reason when present), then apply the tracker's 'needs-decision' label so a human or the next lap can re-open the question — never silently. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"closed_pending": true, "class": "<premise-dead|stand-down>", "note": "<one line>"}

until_argv:
import os, subprocess, sys, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path('.')
bases = sorted(root.glob('**/checkout.baseline'))
r = os.environ.get('WF_B2P_REPO', '.')
cur = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', r, 'status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=all'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
base = bases[0].read_text() if bases else ''
sys.exit(0 if len(bases) == 1 and cur == base else 1)

nodes.context: Zero-token fail-closed law: this gate releases ONLY when exactly one intake snapshot is found in the run tree and the worktree matches it (empty delta vs the snapshot; the repo comes from WF_B2P_REPO). It times out red after 300s — a machine timeout is a failure, not an approval; the run stays parked honestly for the next lap to inspect.
